clue.text: Page races around — impossible distance to cover!

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of races are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic dash past a page, covering an impossible distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns RACES into ARSEC. The definition is playful: a parsec is about 3.26 light years, a distance nobody could cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of length, roughly 3.26 light years, far beyond any journey.

clue.text: Meet son in a drunken state? Gosh!

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Meeting one's son while plastered is cause for exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a drunken state' rearranges MEETSON. The question mark flags the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, an informal British idiom.

clue.text: Surveys revealing no more battered wives

parts.note: something that is over is finished, no more

indicators.note: battered implies being knocked out of shape, so the letters of wives are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reports announcing an end to domestic violence against wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' turns WIVES into VIEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys and overviews are both general looks over a whole subject, plural nouns.

clue.text: A person taking the mickey without anxiety

parts.note: a tease is a person who mocks or ribs others, taking the mickey in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone ribbing others feels perfectly relaxed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the mickey' is British slang for teasing or mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed, free of worry, is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Youngster is first to mimic art form

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the word mimic

explanation.surface: A child who is the first to copy an artistic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism is the early twentieth-century painting movement of Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Instructions order fellow to break discs

indicators.note: to break means getting into the middle, splitting the discs apart

parts.note: CDs are compact discs
OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Orders given for a man to smash some records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' places OM and MAN inside CDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Commands are orders or directives, plural nouns as instructions are.

clue.text: Deceive a bank

definitions.meaning: to mislead someone by pretending, as in poker
a steep cliff or headland is called this

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means fooling by false confidence; the noun means a broad steep slope or cliff face.

clue.text: Listener's broken into country compound

indicators.note: broken into means one piece has forced its way inside another

parts.note: a state is a country
the ear is the organ of listening; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A burglar who eavesdrops has raided a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken into' puts EAR inside STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stearate is a chemical salt or ester of stearic acid, a compound.

clue.text: Cat I, a vet, managed to get going

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and reorganised

explanation.surface: A vet manages to get a cat moving again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges CATIAVET.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something working or in motion; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Charges I'm to render to, initially, every subscriber

parts.note: to put something into words is to render it

indicators.note: initially signals taking the opening letters of every and subscriber

explanation.surface: A fee that I must pass on to each subscriber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes E and S from 'every subscriber'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute or ascribe blame, as one charges a person with something.

clue.text: It's more sensible as an error's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Owning up to a mistake is the wiser course.
explanation.definitionFit: Saner is the comparative of sane, meaning of sounder judgement.

clue.text: Hurries back across time for Shakespeare's home

indicators.note: across means the outer word stretches over the others, enclosing them
back means the word for hurries is read in reverse

parts.note: darts means hurries, moving quickly

explanation.surface: Rushing back through time to visit the Bard's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DARTS into STRAD; 'across' puts T and FOR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratford-upon-Avon is the English town where the playwright was born and lived.

clue.text: Attempt to get vessel from larder

indicators.note: from means the vessel is removed out of the larder

parts.note: a pantry is a larder
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Trying to fetch a pot out of the store cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes PAN from PANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a go or effort; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Politician in twist about spinning? One must get things together

indicators.note: in places the politician inside the twist

parts.note: a coil is a twist or loop
MP stands for Member of Parliament

indicators.note: spinning means the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A politician twisting and spinning while trying to pull things together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MP inside COIL; 'spinning' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who compiles assembles material together, like the setter of this crossword.

clue.text: Delicate daughter isn't needing mummy finally

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of mummy

explanation.surface: A fragile girl no longer needs her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes Y, the last letter of 'mummy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means fine and delicately small or pretty.

clue.text: Smart dame wandering around capital

indicators.note: wandering around suggests the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A stylish lady strolling about a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering around' rearranges SMARTDAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: What is it you'll find in the drinks cabinet?

definitions.text: What is it you'll find in the drinks cabinet?

parts.words: What is it you'll find in the drinks cabinet?
parts.note: the whole clue reads as a riddle naming one bottle among the drinks, a fortified wine flavoured with herbs

explanation.surface: Someone asking what is kept in the drinks cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is an aromatised fortified wine commonly kept with other spirits and mixers.

clue.text: Interjection unknown in the audience

indicators.note: in the audience means as heard by listeners, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: y is a conventional unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An exclamation from an unidentified spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the audience' says the letter Y is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise or impatience, as in 'Why, it's you!'

clue.text: Very fashionable label on a flat figure

parts.note: hep is an old slang word for very fashionable, a variant of hip
a tag is a label
on is taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy label stuck on a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptagon is a plane shape with seven sides.

clue.text: One million without special or distinctive doctrine

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first pair wraps around the other letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One in a million lacks any special belief system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', placing I and M around S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is any distinctive theory, practice or belief system.

clue.text: Red to revolt against the church

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the church sits beside the revolt

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a rising is a revolt, so rise means revolt

explanation.surface: Socialists rising up against the established church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means up beside, putting CE in front of RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry-coloured shade of red.

clue.text: Publicity person who gets paid for work?

definitions.meaning: a professional, one paid rather than an amateur

explanation.definitionFit: Short for both public relations officer and professional, a paid player.

clue.text: Beam from one who keeps changing opinions

definitions.meaning: a short timber joist that supports others in a floor frame
a person who adjusts views to suit whichever side prevails

explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry the word names a supporting joist; in politics it names a timeserver who shifts allegiance.

clue.text: Like some cottages maybe not needing a sewer?

definitions.meaning: describing a tied cottage where no payment is charged
punning reading: a rent is a tear, and a garment without one needs no one to stitch it

explanation.definitionFit: Housing let without charge; and humorously, free of any tear needing stitching by someone who sews.

clue.text: Girl in the end gets followed

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the end

parts.note: end means the end
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: In the end a girl gets pursued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SUE inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means came after or resulted, a synonym of followed.

clue.text: Eastern boys trapping any number of animals

indicators.note: trapping means holding the number inside the boys

parts.note: lads are boys
n stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Lads from the east catching a herd of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' puts N inside LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes.

clue.text: English mum with people flowing out

parts.note: ma is mum, mother
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An English mother pours out among her countrymen.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something issuing forth from a source, the act of flowing out.

clue.text: Famous people Kentish person possibly upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, reading the letters upwards

parts.note: SE stands for south-east, the region of England where Kent lies
a man is a person

explanation.surface: A man from Kent, perhaps unsettled by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SEMAN round; Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Big names are celebrities, so names stand for famous people.

clue.text: Drink barrels brought to a dance

parts.note: rum is a drink
b is an abbreviation used for barrels

explanation.surface: Kegs of spirit are carried to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Strange sorcerer offers stuff for jumble sale

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange
a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A weird wizard donates items to a charity sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends collected for a charity sale; in America a rummage sale.

clue.text: What school without leadership must do to advance

definitions.text: What school without leadership must do to advance

parts.words: What school without leadership must do to advance
parts.note: a school lacking a principal must appoint one; the phrase also means to progress

explanation.surface: A headless school must recruit to move forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to make progress, and literally to acquire a principal.

clue.text: Elected Canadian national has very old-fashioned socks

indicators.note: has means the outer letters hold the socks inside them

parts.note: CN is Canadian National, the railway company
hose is an archaic word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A Canadian wearing antique hosiery wins the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' puts HOSE inside CN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen means picked or selected, as elected candidates are.
